children: Passenger vehicle sales grew about 36 per cent year-on-year during April-August 2026, while entry-segment sales rose more than 96 per cent

Maruti Suzuki India is accelerating its capital expenditure plans following an increase in passenger vehicle demand after the GST 2.0 rationalisation, Managing Director and CEO Hisashi Takeuchi said on Tuesday, as the tax reform completes one year.

Maruti Suzuki's passenger vehicle sales grew about 36 per cent year-on-year during April-August 2026, while sales in the entry segment increased more than 96 per cent during the period, Takeuchi said.

In a post on X, Takeuchi said the increase in entry-segment sales reflected improved affordability following the GST changes. He added that the company was accelerating its capex plans in response to the demand growth.

The GST changes took effect on 22 September 2025. Petrol, LPG and CNG vehicles with engine capacity of up to 1,200 cc and length of up to 4,000 mm, as well as diesel vehicles with engine capacity of up to 1,500 cc and length of up to 4,000 mm, were moved from the 28 per cent GST rate to 18 per cent.

Mahindra and Mahindra has also reported growth across vehicle categories following the tax changes. Rajesh Jejurikar, Executive Director and CEO, Auto and Farm Sector, Mahindra and Mahindra, said SUV sales grew 17 per cent, while light commercial vehicles and tractors grew around 20 per cent.
Jejurikar also said the company plans to add 4,000 units of electric vehicle capacity by March 2027.

The Federation of Automobile Dealers Association (FADA) has reported an increase in auto retail volumes since the GST changes. FADA President Sai Giridhar said auto retail crossed 3 crore vehicles between October 2025 and August 2026, with growth of nearly 20 per cent year-on-year.

Giridhar attributed the increase to improved affordability across vehicle categories, while also noting that manufacturers continue to face cost pressures from fluctuations in crude, commodities and currencies.

The GST rationalisation has therefore coincided with higher demand across passenger vehicles and other automobile segments, while automakers are responding with capacity and capital expenditure plans.
